paper.title_en: The dead-cone effect in charm, bottom and top quark jets in angular and momentum space
paper.abstract_en: The dead-cone effect reflects the mass dependence of QCD radiation from heavy quarks. We investigate this phenomenon from charm and bottom to top quarks using two-dimensional angular distributions and single-particle inclusive momentum spectra. The angular distributions illustrate the depletion of radiation around the heavy-quark direction, while the momentum spectra provide a quantitative observable of the effect. For charm and bottom jets, fragmentation functions reconstructed from LEP data at the $Z$ pole exhibit a strong suppression of high-momentum particles, quantitatively described within the Modified Leading Logarithmic Approximation of perturbative QCD. The analysis is extended to $\sqrt{s}=1$ TeV using Monte Carlo simulations. A hypothetical stable-top sample isolates the primary top-quark radiation pattern, whereas the physical decay $t\to bW$ introduces coherent radiation from the $tb$ colour dipole, obscuring the primary dead cone. By exploiting the dependence on the $b$-quark emission angle $Θ_b$, we reconstruct the primary top-quark parton momentum spectrum through extrapolation to $Θ_b\to0$. In contrast, the small-angle gluon and parton distributions do not converge to the stable-top dead-cone pattern because of radiation from the decay $b$ quark. These findings establish the inclusive momentum spectrum as a robust quantitative observable of the top-quark dead-cone effect and provide a unified description of mass-dependent QCD radiation from charm to top.
